title: cerastium pauciflorum var. amurense
intro: Cerastium pauciflorum var. amurense, commonly known as the Amur mouse-ear chickweed, is a type of flowering plant in the carnation family (Caryophyllaceae). It is a perennial herb native to the temperate regions of Asia, known for its medicinal properties and health benefits. The plant has been traditionally used to treat various health conditions, including fever, rheumatism, and digestive issues, due to its therapeutic actions of anti-inflammatory, antioxidant, and antiseptic properties. The bioactive constituents of Cerastium pauciflorum var. amurense include flavonoids, alkaloids, and phenolic acids, which contribute to its medicinal properties and potential health benefits.
